{\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n    \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr Option `i` is built from its global index, so no options are scattered from rank 0.\n  - Prices are gathered to rank 0 in global order with `MPI_Gatherv`. Sum, min/max, samples, the FNV hash and validation all run there, on the same sequence as before, so results are bit-identical.\n  - Timing is `MPI_Barrier` before the pricing loop, then the slowest rank's time via `MPI_Reduce(MAX)`.\n  - Only rank 0 prints. The executable name is unchanged.\n\n**Verification**\n\n- Built the original and the new version side by side and compared output. For option counts 0, 1, 3, 10, 11, 1000, 1000003 and 1000000, at 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 16 ranks, all sums, min/max, samples, hashes, validation lines and exit codes match. This keeps the pricing work observable, as in the original.\n- The hash and stats stay serial on rank 0. FNV-1a can't be combined across ranks without changing the hash, and the O(N) pass is cheap next to pricing.\n\nI didn't commit anything.
